channel.title: AI Daily Watch: all topics
channel.description: Daily Microsoft, Copilot and AI news.

item.title: Claude Code contributor Thariq says he has left Anthropic
item.description: Anthropic: Thariq publicly said he had left Anthropic after more than a year working on Claude Code. His post thanked colleagues and the Claude Code community; it is notable personnel news related to Claude Code, though it does not announce a product change.

item.title: Pennsylvania adopts disclosure labels for qualifying AI-generated ads
item.description: Pennsylvania: Pennsylvania enacted a law requiring labels on advertisements that are generated or significantly modified using AI, according to The Verge. The report notes that the law leaves some terms open to interpretation; the governor signed it on October 22, before the monitoring start date.

item.title: Study reports partisan differences in forced candidate recommendations by Grok and OpenAI models
item.description: xAI and OpenAI: A Convovo study reported that, when explicitly forced to recommend a candidate across nearly 500 U.S. midterm races, Grok 4.7 chose Republicans in 92% of its answers and OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol chose Democrats in 97%. The findings raise questions about model behavior and political neutrality, but the article cautions that the test used APIs and an unusually direct prompt, not ordinary chatbot use.

item.title: Block introduces Dessa, a locally runnable full-duplex speech model
item.description: Block: Block introduced Dessa, a full-duplex speech model trained entirely on human speech that can run locally on a consumer computer such as a MacBook M4 Max. The release points toward more natural, on-device voice AI, while Block is seeking safety testing before broader access.

item.title: OpenAI and Poland’s NASK partner on AI safety and security
item.description: OpenAI: OpenAI announced a partnership with Poland’s NASK focused on AI safety, security, and technical research. The collaboration is intended to strengthen safeguards and support a more resilient digital ecosystem; it was published before the monitoring start date.

item.title: Google DeepMind releases a global map of forest types
item.description: Google DeepMind: Google DeepMind and Google Research, working with the World Resources Institute and IIASA, released Forest Typology 2020, a global 10-meter-resolution map distinguishing six forest and land-use types. They also shared an early time series tracking changes from 2017 to 2025, including natural forests converted to plantations or farms.
